If you're a fresher in 2026, don't compete with AI. Learn to work with it. 🤖

A lot of freshers are worried:

“Will AI make entry-level developers irrelevant?”

I think the better question is:

“Can I become the fresher who knows how to use AI better than the other candidates?”

Because companies still need people who can:

→ Understand a problem
→ Break it into smaller pieces
→ Write and debug code
→ Understand APIs, databases & systems
→ Review AI-generated code
→ Ask the right questions
→ Explain their decisions clearly

AI can generate code.

But it doesn't automatically give you engineering judgment.

So if you're preparing for your first software job, don't spend all your time learning random AI tools.

Build these 5 things:

1. DSA fundamentals
Know how to think through problems, not just memorize solutions.

2. One solid project
Something you can explain end-to-end: architecture, database, APIs, trade-offs.

3. AI-assisted development
Use AI to understand, debug, test and improve your code — not blindly copy it.

4. Core CS fundamentals
OOP, DBMS, OS, networking and basic system design still matter.

5. Communication
Being able to explain why you built something a certain way is becoming even more valuable.

The goal isn't:

❌ “I know ChatGPT.”

The goal is:

✅ “I can solve engineering problems, and AI helps me do it faster.”

Don't try to become an AI expert before becoming a good engineer.

Become a good engineer who knows how to leverage AI.

That's a much stronger career advantage.
